WEB-1801 (S3). Privacy §7's first bullet (`en.ts:122`, `es.ts:122`, `ca.ts:122`) says personal content is kept ‘until you delete the content or account’ and that ‘Deleting an individual item can leave synchronisation metadata’. In fact the server keeps the whole deleted row, hidden. Deleting a task or a note only marks it deleted (`../TaskFlow/Backend/core/task_views.py:108-120`; a note is a task of kind note, `../TaskFlow/Backend/core/models.py:199`), and deleting a project does the same to every task in it (`../TaskFlow/Backend/core/list_views.py:232-246`); only the files are removed. The row keeps its title, notes, checklist and dates, and since the app's D2 its completion times (`../TaskFlow/Backend/docs/COMPLETION_TIMES.md:11-12`). Nothing purges it (`../TaskFlow/Backend/core/management/commands/maintain_staging.py:10`: ‘Never deletes tasks or attachments’). It goes only with the account (`../TaskFlow/Backend/docs/ACCOUNT_DELETION.md:21`, ‘soft-deleted rows included’), and in a continuing shared project it stays with the project (`../TaskFlow/Backend/core/account_deletion.py:78`). Replace the whole bullet, exactly: EN `Account and personal cloud content: kept while you have your account. We never delete your tasks on our own, done or not. A task, note or project you delete leaves your devices and its files are removed, but our server keeps the rest of it, hidden, until you delete your account (if it was in a shared project, it stays with that project). Account deletion removes your personal database records and sessions.` / ES `Cuenta y contenido personal en la nube: se conservan mientras tengas la cuenta. Nunca borramos tus tareas por nuestra cuenta, estén hechas o no. Una tarea, nota o proyecto que borras desaparece de tus dispositivos y se eliminan sus archivos, pero nuestro servidor guarda el resto, oculto, hasta que elimines tu cuenta (si estaba en un proyecto compartido, se queda con ese proyecto). Eliminar la cuenta suprime sus registros personales en la base de datos y sus sesiones.` / CA `Compte i contingut personal al núvol: es conserven mentre tinguis el compte. No esborrem mai les teves tasques pel nostre compte, fetes o no. Una tasca, nota o projecte que esborres desapareix dels teus dispositius i se’n suprimeixen els fitxers, però el nostre servidor en conserva la resta, oculta, fins que suprimeixis el compte (si era en un projecte compartit, es queda amb aquell projecte). Suprimir el compte elimina els registres personals de la base de dades i les sessions.` This is review L's copy with one change of the organizer's, in ES and CA only: the subjunctive ‘hasta que elimines’ / ‘fins que suprimeixis’ for an event still to come, as ‘mientras tengas’ / ‘mentre tinguis’ in the same bullet (the review wrote ‘eliminas’ / ‘suprimeixes’).

decisions.question: How long should a task, note or project someone deletes stay on the server?
decisions.recommendation: (b) before launch: a scheduled server job removes the content of deleted tasks, notes and projects after a set time (for example 30 days, like the server logs) and keeps only the ‘deleted’ mark that offline phones need, as `../TaskFlow/Backend/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:92, 110` already plans. It's server work through the app's loop, not the site's; privacy §7 then names the period in a later legal version. Until it ships, WP268's copy says what happens today.
decisions.context: Review L's Q-L1, raised with WEB-1801 and filed as WEB-1804 in review L's number block (it had no ID). Today a deleted task, note or project is only marked deleted: the server keeps its title, notes, checklist, dates and, since D2, its completion times, hidden, until the account is deleted, and in a continuing shared project it stays with the project; only its files go (`../TaskFlow/Backend/core/task_views.py:108-120`, `list_views.py:232-246`, `management/commands/maintain_staging.py:10`; `../TaskFlow/Backend/docs/ACCOUNT_DELETION.md:21`). (a) Keep that, and the site says so (WP268's copy, which ships either way). (b) A server job removes their content after a set time and keeps only the tombstone; the site then names the period. Storage limitation (GDPR art. 5(1)(e)) is a legal check for the WD3 sign-off. It sits beside the app's open item ‘Cleaning up completed tasks’ (`../TaskFlow/.claude/ux-review/DECISIONS.md`, Open; `../TaskFlow/Backend/docs/ACCOUNT_DELETION.md`, item 3): both could be answered as one retention policy, which `ARCHITECTURE.md`'s checklist still lists as not approved. Under (b), §7's ‘We never delete your tasks on our own, done or not.’ still holds for tasks the person hasn't deleted; the later legal version must say so plainly.
